lines.title: Modern: 2...Qxd5 3.Nc3 Qd6
lines.pgn: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qd6 4. d4 Nf6 5. Nf3 a6 6. Be2 Bf5 7. O-O e6 8. Be3 Be7
lines.lineSummary: The Modern Scandinavian with ...Qd6 — the most popular and solid choice. Black develops harmoniously.
lines.strategicGoal: Place the queen on d6 where it supports ...e6, ...Bf5, and ...Be7 development. Solid and reliable.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays aggressively with Bf4 too early, allowing ...Qb4+ or ...Nc6 with tempo.
lines.punishmentIdea: After premature Bf4, ...Nc6 attacks d4. If d5, ...Nb4 threatens Nc2+ forking.
lines.hintText: ...Qd6 is the safest square — it supports ...e6 and doesn't block any pieces. Develop ...Bf5 next.

lines.title: Classical: 2...Qxd5 3.Nc3 Qa5
lines.pgn: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qa5 4. d4 Nf6 5. Nf3 Bf5 6. Bc4 e6 7. Bd2 c6 8. Qe2 Bb4
lines.lineSummary: The Classical Scandinavian with ...Qa5 — more active than ...Qd6 but requires more precision.
lines.strategicGoal: Queen on a5 pins the Nc3 to the king. Develop ...Bf5, ...c6, ...e6 for a solid position.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Bd2 too early, allowing ...Bb4 pinning the knight and increasing pressure.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Bb4, the Nc3 is pinned twice (queen + bishop). White must be very careful.
lines.hintText: ...Qa5 is more active but riskier. The queen pins Nc3 and supports ...Bb4 later.

lines.title: Icelandic Gambit: 2...Nf6
lines.pgn: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Nf6 3. c4 e6 4. dxe6 Bxe6 5. d4 Bb4+ 6. Nc3 O-O 7. Be2 Re8
lines.lineSummary: The Icelandic Gambit — Black sacrifices a pawn for rapid development and pressure on White's center.
lines.strategicGoal: After ...Nf6 and ...e6, sacrifice the pawn for fast development. ...Bb4+ and ...Re8 create pressure.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White grabs the pawn with c4 and dxe6, falling behind in development.
lines.punishmentIdea: After dxe6 Bxe6, Black has a lead in development. ...Bb4+, ...O-O, ...Re8 create real threats.
lines.hintText: The Icelandic Gambit works when White is greedy. After ...e6 dxe6 Bxe6, you have great development.

lines.title: 2...Nf6: Portuguese Variation
lines.pgn: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Nf6 3. d4 Bg4 4. Nf3 Qxd5 5. Be2 Nc6 6. O-O O-O-O 7. c4 Qa5 8. Be3
lines.lineSummary: The Portuguese/Jadoul variation — Black plays ...Nf6 first, developing the bishop to g4 before recapturing.
lines.strategicGoal: Develop ...Bg4 before taking back on d5. Castle queenside for an aggressive setup against White's king.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Be2 passively, allowing Black to castle queenside with a strong attack.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...O-O-O, Black has a ready-made kingside attack with ...h5-h4 and piece pressure.
lines.hintText: 2...Nf6 followed by ...Bg4 is the aggressive Scandinavian. Castle queenside for attacking chances.

lines.title: vs 3.d4 4.Nf3: Standard White
lines.pgn: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qd6 4. d4 Nf6 5. Nf3 c6 6. Ne5 Nbd7 7. Nc4 Qc7 8. Bf4 Qb8
lines.lineSummary: Against White's most natural setup (d4+Nf3), Black plays ...c6 and reroutes the queen if needed.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...c6 to support ...Bf5 and prepare ...e6. If White plays Ne5, ...Nbd7 challenges it.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Ne5 without support, allowing ...Nbd7 to challenge and exchange.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Nbd7 Nc4 Qc7, the knight on c4 can be pushed back with ...b5 gaining space.
lines.hintText: Against Ne5, play ...Nbd7 to challenge immediately. Don't let White keep a knight on e5.

lines.title: Trap: Fishing Pole Attack
lines.pgn: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qa5 4. d4 Nf6 5. Nf3 Bg4 6. h3 Bh5 7. g4 Bg6 8. Ne5 e6 9. Bg2 c6 10. h4
lines.lineSummary: A dangerous trap where White overextends with g4-h4, and Black can exploit the weakened kingside.
lines.strategicGoal: Provoke White into g4-h4 overextension, then exploit the weakened kingside with ...Nbd7 and ...O-O-O.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White pushes g4 and h4 aggressively, weakening their own king position.
lines.punishmentIdea: After g4 h4, White's king is exposed. ...Nbd7 and ...O-O-O gives Black a safer king and attack.
lines.hintText: If White plays g4 trying to win your bishop, don't panic. Their kingside is now full of holes.

lines.title: Solid: 2...Qxd5 3.Nc3 Qd8
lines.pgn: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qd8 4. d4 Nf6 5. Nf3 Bg4 6. Be2 e6 7. O-O Be7 8. h3 Bh5 9. Be3 O-O
lines.lineSummary: The ultra-solid ...Qd8 retreat — gives up tempo but avoids all queen harassment.
lines.strategicGoal: Retreat to d8 for maximum safety. Develop ...Bg4, ...e6, ...Be7 and castle quickly.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White assumes the tempo advantage is decisive, but Black's position is very solid.
lines.punishmentIdea: Black's position is rock-solid. After ...O-O, the position is balanced despite the tempo loss.
lines.hintText: ...Qd8 is the safest but slowest. Use it when you want a solid, risk-free game.

lines.title: vs 2.c4: Panov-like Structure
lines.pgn: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Nf6 3. c4 c6 4. dxc6 Nxc6 5. Nf3 e5 6. d3 Bc5 7. Be2 O-O 8. O-O
lines.lineSummary: When White plays 2.c4 trying to hold the pawn, Black gets active piece play with ...c6 and ...e5.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...c6 to undermine the d5 pawn. After dxc6 Nxc6, develop actively with ...e5 and ...Bc5.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White holds the d5 pawn too long with c4, falling behind in development.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...c6 dxc6 Nxc6, Black has rapid development and ...e5 gives a strong center.
lines.hintText: Against 2.c4, play ...c6! to undermine. After Nxc6, you have great development and ...e5.

lines.title: Gubinsky Countergambit: 3...Qe5+
lines.pgn: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qe5+ 4. Be2 c6 5. Nf3 Qc7 6. d4 Nf6 7. O-O Bf5 8. Bf4 Qb6
lines.lineSummary: An unusual queen placement on e5 with check, disrupting White's development.
lines.strategicGoal: ...Qe5+ forces Be2 (blocking the bishop's best square). Then ...Qc7 and normal development.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White blocks with Be2, which is passive. The bishop belongs on c4 or d3.
lines.punishmentIdea: By forcing Be2, Black ensures White's bishop is on a passive square. Normal development follows.
lines.hintText: ...Qe5+ is a surprise weapon. It forces Be2 and disrupts White's ideal piece placement.

lines.title: vs 2.Nf3: Anti-Scandinavian
lines.pgn: 1. e4 d5 2. Nf3 dxe4 3. Ng5 Nf6 4. Nc3 Bf5 5. Bc4 e6 6. d3 exd3 7. Qf3 Qd7 8. Qxd3
lines.lineSummary: When White plays 2.Nf3 instead of 2.exd5, Black can grab the pawn and defend it.
lines.strategicGoal: After 2.Nf3 dxe4, hold the extra pawn with ...Nf6 and ...Bf5. Develop solidly.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Ng5 too early without enough support, allowing Black to consolidate.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Bf5 and ...e6, the extra pawn is secure. Black develops naturally and keeps material.
lines.hintText: Against 2.Nf3, take the pawn! After ...dxe4, defend with ...Nf6 and ...Bf5.

lines.title: Advance: 3.e5 Main Line
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. e5 c5 4. c3 Nc6 5. Nf3 Qb6 6. Be2 cxd4 7. cxd4 Nh6 8. Nc3 Nf5 9. Na4 Qa5+
lines.lineSummary: Against the Advance (3.e5), Black attacks the d4 pawn base with ...c5 and pressures the center.
lines.strategicGoal: Attack the pawn chain base with ...c5. Develop ...Nc6, ...Qb6 pressuring d4 and b2.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays c3 without Nf3, allowing ...Qb6 to hit both b2 and d4 simultaneously.
lines.punishmentIdea: ...Qb6 attacks b2 and d4. White must choose which to defend, often making concessions.
lines.hintText: Against the Advance, always play ...c5 immediately! Attack the base of the pawn chain.

lines.title: Winawer: 3.Nc3 Bb4 Main Line
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Bb4 4. e5 c5 5. a3 Bxc3+ 6. bxc3 Ne7 7. Qg4 Qc7 8. Qxg7 Rg8 9. Qxh7 cxd4
lines.lineSummary: The Winawer — Black pins Nc3 with ...Bb4, leading to extremely sharp play. A Botvinnik favorite.
lines.strategicGoal: Pin Nc3 with ...Bb4, then after e5, attack the center with ...c5. Accept structural damage for activity.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White grabs pawns with Qxg7 and Qxh7, losing time while Black gets massive center play.
lines.punishmentIdea: While White's queen grabs pawns, Black plays ...cxd4 opening the center with a huge lead in development.
lines.hintText: The Winawer is sharp — after ...Bb4 and ...c5, you sacrifice structure for dynamic piece play.

lines.title: Classical: 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Be7 5. e5 Nfd7 6. Bxe7 Qxe7 7. f4 O-O 8. Nf3 c5 9. Qd2 Nc6
lines.lineSummary: The Classical French with ...Nf6 and 4.Bg5 — solid and well-tested at all levels.
lines.strategicGoal: After e5 Nfd7, exchange bishops with Bxe7 Qxe7. Then attack d4 with ...c5 and ...Nc6.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White pushes f4-f5 too early without securing the center, allowing ...cxd4 with tempo.
lines.punishmentIdea: After premature f5, ...cxd4 opens the center while White's f-pawn is overextended.
lines.hintText: In the Classical, after ...Nfd7, play ...c5 ASAP. The d4 pawn is your target.

lines.title: Tarrasch: 3.Nd2 Main Line
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nd2 c5 4. exd5 exd5 5. Ngf3 Nc6 6. Bb5 Bd6 7. dxc5 Bxc5 8. O-O Nge7 9. Nb3 Bd6
lines.lineSummary: Against the Tarrasch (3.Nd2), Black plays ...c5 and gets an IQP position with active pieces.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...c5 to open the position. After exd5 exd5, use the IQP dynamically with piece activity.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White exchanges too early with dxc5, giving Black free development and the bishop pair.
lines.punishmentIdea: After dxc5 Bxc5, Black has rapid development and the IQP provides dynamic chances.
lines.hintText: Against 3.Nd2, play ...c5 immediately. The IQP positions favor active piece play.

lines.title: Exchange: 3.exd5 exd5
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. exd5 exd5 4. Nf3 Nf6 5. Bd3 Bd6 6. O-O O-O 7. Bg5 Bg4 8. Nbd2 Nbd7 9. c3 c6
lines.lineSummary: The Exchange French — symmetrical but Black can play for a win with active piece play.
lines.strategicGoal: Develop naturally with ...Bd6, ...O-O, ...Bg4. Aim for ...Re8 and ...Ne4 for activity.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays too passively in the symmetrical position, allowing Black to seize the initiative.
lines.punishmentIdea: In the Exchange, Black can play for ...Ne4 and ...f5 to create kingside chances.
lines.hintText: The Exchange French is drawish but playable. Aim for ...Bg4, ...Re8, and ...Ne4 for activity.

lines.title: Advance: Milner-Barry Gambit
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. e5 c5 4. c3 Nc6 5. Nf3 Qb6 6. Bd3 cxd4 7. cxd4 Bd7 8. O-O Nxd4 9. Nxd4 Qxd4 10. Nc3
lines.lineSummary: The Milner-Barry Gambit where White sacrifices d4 for rapid development. Black must be precise.
lines.strategicGoal: Accept the d4 pawn sacrifice but be ready for White's rapid development. ...Bd7 and ...O-O-O are key.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black takes d4 without preparing ...Bd7, falling behind in development.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Nxd4 Nxd4 Qxd4, White plays Nc3 with rapid development and threats against the queen.
lines.hintText: You CAN take the d4 pawn, but develop ...Bd7 first. Don't get greedy without preparation.

lines.title: Rubinstein: 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nd7 5. Nf3 Ngf6 6. Nxf6+ Nxf6 7. Bd3 c5 8. dxc5 Bxc5 9. O-O O-O
lines.lineSummary: The Rubinstein variation — Black exchanges in the center early for a solid, easy-to-play position.
lines.strategicGoal: Exchange on e4 to eliminate the cramping pawn. Develop ...Nd7, ...Ngf6, ...c5 for equality.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Nxf6+ too early, helping Black develop the other knight.
lines.punishmentIdea: After Nxf6+ Nxf6, Black has easy development. ...c5 equalizes the center completely.
lines.hintText: The Rubinstein is the easiest French to play. Exchange on e4, develop, and equalize.

lines.title: Advance: ...Bd7 Euwe Plan
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. e5 c5 4. c3 Nc6 5. Nf3 Bd7 6. Be2 Nge7 7. Na3 cxd4 8. cxd4 Nf5 9. Nc2 Qb6
lines.lineSummary: The Euwe plan with ...Bd7 and ...Nge7-f5 — a solid alternative to the main line ...Qb6.
lines.strategicGoal: Develop ...Bd7, ...Nge7, then ...Nf5 attacking d4. A more positional approach than ...Qb6.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White ignores the Nf5 pressure on d4, allowing ...Nfxd4 with advantage.
lines.punishmentIdea: ...Nf5 hits d4 directly. If White doesn't defend carefully, ...Nfxd4 wins a pawn.
lines.hintText: The Euwe plan (...Bd7, ...Nge7-f5) is more solid than ...Qb6. The knight on f5 pressures d4.

lines.title: Korchnoi Gambit: 3.Nd2 c5 4.Ngf3 cxd4
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nd2 c5 4. Ngf3 cxd4 5. exd5 Qxd5 6. Bc4 Qd6 7. O-O Nf6 8. Nb3 Nc6 9. Nbxd4 Nxd4 10. Nxd4 a6
lines.lineSummary: A dynamic approach where Black captures on d4 early, accepting an IQP for active piece play.
lines.strategicGoal: After ...cxd4 and ...Qxd5, use the open lines for piece activity. The IQP provides dynamic chances.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Bc4 too early, allowing ...Qd6 with tempo on the bishop.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Qd6, the queen is well-placed supporting ...e5 and ...Bc5 development.
lines.hintText: After ...cxd4, accept the IQP. Your pieces will be active enough to compensate.

lines.title: Trap: Advance ...Bg4 Pin
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. e5 c5 4. c3 Nc6 5. Nf3 Bg4 6. Be2 cxd4 7. cxd4 Bxf3 8. Bxf3 Nxd4 9. Bxb7 Rb8
lines.lineSummary: A tactical trap in the Advance where Black pins the Nf3 and wins the d4 pawn.
lines.strategicGoal: Pin the knight with ...Bg4, then after ...cxd4 cxd4, exchange on f3 and take d4 with the knight.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays cxd4 without noticing the ...Bxf3 Bxf3 Nxd4 tactic.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Bxf3 Bxf3 Nxd4, Black wins a pawn. White's bishop on b7 is trapped after ...Rb8.
lines.hintText: In the Advance, ...Bg4 can be a tactical weapon. If White is careless, you win the d4 pawn.

lines.title: McCutcheon: 4.Bg5 Bb4
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Bb4 5. e5 h6 6. Bd2 Bxc3 7. bxc3 Ne4 8. Qg4 g6 9. Bd3 Nxd2 10. Kxd2
lines.lineSummary: The McCutcheon — Black plays ...Bb4 against Bg5, creating complex imbalanced positions.
lines.strategicGoal: Pin Nc3 with ...Bb4 and after e5, play ...h6 and ...Ne4 to create complications.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays e5 without preparation, allowing ...h6 Bd2 Bxc3 with structural damage.
lines.punishmentIdea: After bxc3, White has doubled c-pawns and a weakened structure. Black's ...Ne4 is very strong.
lines.hintText: The McCutcheon (...Bb4 against Bg5) creates chaos. After ...h6 and ...Ne4, you have active play.

lines.title: Advance: Nimzovich ...Nh6 Plan
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. e5 c5 4. c3 Nc6 5. Nf3 Nh6 6. Bd3 cxd4 7. cxd4 Nf5 8. Bxf5 exf5 9. O-O Be6
lines.lineSummary: The Nimzovich plan with ...Nh6-f5 — the knight reroutes to attack d4 and control key squares.
lines.strategicGoal: Play ...Nh6 to reroute to f5, attacking d4. After Bxf5 exf5, Black has the bishop pair and open e-file.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White exchanges Bxf5 exf5, opening the e-file for Black's rook and giving the bishop pair.
lines.punishmentIdea: After Bxf5 exf5, Black's bishop pair and open e-file provide lasting compensation.
lines.hintText: ...Nh6-f5 is the Nimzovich plan. The knight attacks d4 and if exchanged, opens the e-file.
